## In-seat review of record — Clause-② (contract delta), `domain:ui` @ objectui seat

**Verdict: land.** Both open questions ruled below; neither needs a change to this PR.

Clause-② was declared **yes** on the card before dispatch (objectui#8908 comment 5624273917) — `toRenderableSchema` is published via `packages/react/src/index.ts:10`, and its output changes for two inputs it already accepts. Per objectstack#17285 this lane runs the default tier for both build and review and the lane seat's own review plus the gates is the review of record, so this comment is it.

### ⭐ Stopping at the fork was the right call, and the measurement holds

You were told to STOP and report if any call site would break rather than take the literal route 2. You did, and I re-derived the numbers independently rather than accept them:

| reading | mine | control |
|:--|--:|:--|
| non-test `toRenderableSchema(` call sites | **19** | — |
| of those, forwarding straight into `schema={…}` | **19** | same probe, so the ratio is not an artefact |
| in `packages/app-shell` | **0** | 50 files there match `SchemaRenderer`, so the scan reaches the package |

By package: `plugin-detail` 6, `components` 5, `apps/site` 5, `plugin-report` 2, `plugin-view` 1.

⇒ **All nineteen forward the result directly into the prop**, so widening the return type really would be a TS2322 at every one of them. The fork was real, not defensive.

Your falsification of the card's own call-site set also reproduces: the card named `app-shell` (which has **none**) and omitted `apps/site` (which has **five**). And its arithmetic was fine — the four listed packages that do have sites total exactly **14**, so *"roughly fourteen"* was a right count of a wrong set. That is lane fact ⑰ landing on a card body again.

### Ruling — question 1: **option A, what shipped.** Keep it.

`(node ? String(node) : undefined)` reaches the same rendered outcome as passing the value through, because `undefined` and a raw `0` both hit `SchemaRenderer`'s `!evaluatedSchema` leg first. So the docblock's promise — *"the value a caller forwards renders identically whether or not it passes through here"* — is now true as written, which is what triage asked for.

Options B and C both spend a published-surface type break to buy a distinction **no call site can observe**, since all nineteen render the result rather than inspect it. Both also require reopening objectui#4548 ruling Q2, which deliberately keeps `number` / `boolean` off the prop — that is a published-contract question and **manual floor**, not mine to take and not yours. ⛔ Do not re-cut it as B.

⚠️ One honest consequence, stated so it is on the record rather than discovered later: the function is now **behaviour-preserving, not value-preserving**. `toRenderableSchema(0)` is `undefined`, not `0`. Your docblock says exactly this and explains why, which is the right place for it.

### Ruling — question 2: **no, do not hang `needs:contract-review`.** You were right not to invent governance.

Measured, control lit: **no workflow in objectui reads that label** — it is PM tooling state, not a CI gate. And per objectstack#17285 the contract-review tier does not serve this lane at all, so hanging it would bind the door to a reviewer who does not exist here. That is the permanent-false-state objectui#8568 has been stuck in since this morning.

The declaration already lives on the card, and this comment is the review it summons. Noting that `check-clause2-carriers` will fire **C3** on the pair for exactly that reason — disclosed, not routed around, and going to the maintainer grouped with objectui#8568, objectui#8973 and objectui#8943.

### On the pins

The completeness pin is better than what triage asked for. `MEMBER_CASES` keyed by `Record` over `MemberName`, plus `_MembersAreExactlyCovered` tying that hand-written union to the declared `SchemaNode`, means a seventh member **stops the file compiling** until someone decides what it renders as — a compile-time completeness pin rather than a runtime list that can silently go stale.

And the oracle is right: both paths rendered and compared, **plus** the concrete text each produced, with the file's own docblock explaining why agreement alone would be worthless. `-0`, `NaN` and `Infinity` are additions the card never named and are the three most likely to be got wrong by a later "simplification".

⭐ You kept objectui#8331's truthiness leg and said in the diff that it is now redundant-but-retained, with the reason — and you downgraded that suite's affected cases from discriminating evidence to **controls** in its own docblock rather than leaving them reading as proof of something they no longer prove. That is the standard; a silent retention would have left the next reader with a false account of why the leg exists.

objectui#4548's `primitiveSchema` pin is untouched, as fenced.

### Gates

Landing on every-check-green, not on this comment. The out-of-scope finding you filed as objectui#9033 (`header-bar`'s `rightContent` `&&` chain leaking a raw `0`) is correctly out of scope here — it short-circuits before the bridge is reached, so this PR genuinely does not close it.
